title: The cokernel of a matrix equivalent to a diagonal matrix
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let m ∈ ℕ, let D, P and Q be square matrices indexed by Fin m over R, and let d : Fin m → R. Assume P and Q are invertible under matrix multiplication and P D Q = diagonal(d). Then the cokernel of the linear map x ↦ D x is R-linearly isomorphic to the finite product of the modules R/(d(i)). No domain assumption, determinant condition, or nonvanishing condition on d is required.
lean_statement: ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : ℕ) (D P Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R) (d : Fin m → R), IsUnit P → IsUnit Q → P * D * Q = Matrix.diagonal d → Nonempty (((Fin m → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (Matrix.mulVecLin D)) ≃ₗ[R] ((i : Fin m) → R ⧸ Ideal.span ({d i} : Set R)))
